notes.meaning: Inside the belly of the great fish, Jonah turned to the Lord his God in prayer. Even though he had been running away from God, he still remembered that God was his God and called upon him. God miraculously preserved his life in this dark place so he could seek the Lord. No place is too strange or too dark for God's people to pray to him.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some critical scholars argue that this prayer was a later poem added during or after the Jewish exile, rather than a song written by Jonah himself.

notes.meaning: Jonah cried out to the Lord from his deep distress, and God answered him. He felt as if he were in the belly of the grave, completely cut off from the land of the living. Yet even from those dark depths, God heard his voice and answered his desperate cry. God hears our prayers even when our trouble feels as hopeless as death.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some popular teachers hold that Jonah actually died of drowning and his soul went to the place of the dead before God raised him back to life.

notes.meaning: Jonah recognized that it was God who cast him into the heart of the raging sea, not just the sailors. The ocean currents swirled around him, and all the crashing waves rolled right over him. He saw these terrifying waters as God's own waves sent to correct him. When trials come, believers should recognize God's hand guiding their circumstances.

Jonah felt driven out of God's sight, which was the very thing he had foolishly sought when running away. Yet in the middle of this despair, his faith revived and he resolved to look once more toward God's holy temple. Even when we feel far from God, we can still turn our eyes back to him in trusting prayer.

The raging waters closed completely over Jonah, threatening to put an end to his physical life. As he sank down into the deep sea, thick seaweed wrapped tightly around his head. Everything around him pointed toward certain drowning with no human way of escape.

Jonah sank down to the very foundations of the mountains beneath the ocean. It seemed as though the earth had locked its heavy iron bars behind him forever, sealing him into the world of the dead. But the Lord his God reached down and pulled his life back up from the pit.

As Jonah's life was fading away and he felt completely helpless, he turned his thoughts to the Lord. His earnest prayer rose from the depths and reached God in his holy dwelling place. God never fails to hear the cries of his people, no matter how weak they feel.

Those who cling to worthless idols turn their backs on the true God, who is the fountain of all loving mercy. By trusting in empty things, people throw away the grace and help God was ready to give them. Jonah saw that his own disobedience was like turning toward an empty lie.

Jonah promised to offer sacrifices with songs of thanksgiving and pay the promises he had made to God. He confessed that deliverance from physical danger and from sin comes from the Lord alone. True rescue belongs entirely to God's mercy and power.

The Lord gave the command, and the great fish spat Jonah safely onto the dry land. God showed his absolute power over all nature by directing the creature to preserve and release his servant. This miraculous deliverance also serves as a picture of Christ rising alive from the grave on the third day.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Jonah coming out of the fish alive on the third day is seen as a prophetic picture of Jesus rising from the dead on the third day.
